items.title: Omer Simeon Interview, 1955-08-18
items.q: Then Kidd Ory, and eventually Bonnie and I left. Then we joined Charlie Elger in Milwaukee.

ctx.x: On the alto sax. The three joined us in St. Louis. And from there we went to New York. We stayed around New York, what, a month, a couple of months or so. Played an engagement at the Savoy for two weeks. Then, after we finished the Savoy, Joe didn't have a very good booking agent. So it was really a struggle then, keeping the band together. And they started leaving, one by one, coming back to Chicago. I think Clarence Black was the first one to leave. Then Kidd Ory, and eventually Bonnie and I left. Then we…
Was he still playing pretty well then?

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: we got stranded and when I left there Omer Simeon was the first lead alto

ctx.x: -- from Chicago. You see, we was on the road and we got stranded and when I left there Omer Simeon was the first lead alto and we got stranded in Baltimore. And, finally, the guy gave a dance, and we didn't have any money or

nothing. I ate hot dogs for three days straight. And we were staying in this rooming house, this lodging. The woman began to cook cabbage and hot dogs, and I never ate cabbage in my life. I didn't like it. But then when I began to get hungry after three days of hot dogs, I ate An everything. I ate the cabbage and everything she had on that table and it started me to eat cabbage. And that's when the band broke up.

items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: No, he came to Milwaukee when I was with Charlie Elgar. And Omar Simeon was with Charlie Elgar, too.

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…
. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. That's okay. You can cut that off. One. Two. You see, if you count and then pick back the notes up, it screws you up. Yeah. ¶ Thank you.
